image_description: A grey whale surfaces in green ocean water, its dark, mottled back and dorsal knuckles visible just below the surface. In the background, a small boat filled with tourists wearing life vests observes the whale. A person's head and shoulder are visible in the foreground right, looking towards the whale.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is relatively short with arched rostrum and two blowholes on top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The whale's head is submerged or obscured by water spray and angle; blowholes and rostrum shape are not clearly visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Visible portion of the whale’s back shows characteristic mottled grey skin with lighter patches consistent with barnacle/lice coverage.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible dorsal ridge lacks a true fin and instead shows a series of low humps/knuckles, matching grey whale anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only a partial section of the back is visible; full body shape cannot be assessed due to submersion and framing.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Consistent with Head_and_Face checkpoint — visible skin texture and coloration match expected barnacle-covered mottling.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Baleen plates are cream-colored, densely packed in numerous rows along each side.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Mouth is closed and underwater; baleen plates are not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Pectoral fins are submerged and not visible in this view.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Tail is not visible in frame; only mid-back region is shown.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin texture is rough with callosities.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Surface texture appears uneven and bumpy, consistent with callosities and barnacle encrustation typical of grey whales.

artifact_observations.reasoning: Slight smudging or over-smoothness in texture transition between wet skin and water splash; may indicate minor AI blending artifact but could also be motion blur or compression.
Minor warping in boat edge curvature and passenger proportions suggests slight perspective inconsistency, possibly due to generative model struggling with complex occlusions and reflections.
Unnatural uniformity in ripple patterns and lack of fine detail in splashes suggests synthetic water simulation rather than physical fluid dynamics.

selected_experts.reason: Primary class verification expert; must confirm taxonomic identity at species level using ViT features.
Audit boundary sharpness between whale and water, check for floating fragments or bleeding edges indicative of generation artifacts.
Verify spatial grounding: ensure whale is correctly positioned beneath water surface and boat floats realistically without depth collapse.
Holistic quality scan for subtle degradations, especially in water texture and human figures which often reveal AI artifacts.
Provide bounding box priors for topology auditor; verify object count and placement consistency in crowded scene.
Although limbless, include to detect any anomalous protrusions or impossible structures misinterpreted as limbs by pose estimator.

focus_areas: Whale skin texture fidelity and barnacle pattern realism
Boundary integrity between whale body and surrounding water
Water surface physics and ripple coherence
Boat structure and passenger anatomical plausibility
Depth layering: whale subsurface vs. boat surface positioning
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay special attention to whether the 'dorsal knuckles' are structurally coherent and not fused into a single mass. Verify that the mottling pattern does not repeat unnaturally across the visible surface. Assess if the water interaction (splash, wake) matches the whale’s implied motion vector. Scrutinize human figures for limb fusion or facial distortion — common failure modes in multi-person scenes. Do not ignore low-severity texture anomalies; they may compound into structural implausibility when combined with geometric depth errors.
